title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Strictly Implementing the Open Trial System
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Several Provisions on Strictly Implementing the Open Trial System

Fa Fa [1999] No. 3

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to strictly implement the open trial system, in accordance with the Constitution of the People's Republic of China and relevant laws, the following provisions are hereby made:

1. In conducting trial activities, the people's courts must adhere to the system of open trials according to law, and must hold open court sessions, present evidence and conduct cross-examination openly, and pronounce judgments openly.

2. For cases of first instance, the people's courts shall, in accordance with the law, conduct open trials in all cases except for the following:

   (1) Cases involving state secrets;
   (2) Cases involving personal privacy;
   (3) Cases of crimes committed by minors who have reached the age of 14 but are under the age of 16; and cases of crimes committed by minors who have reached the age of 16 but are under the age of 18, where the people's court has decided not to conduct an open trial;
   (4) Cases involving trade secrets, where the parties have applied and the people's court has decided not to conduct an open trial;
   (5) Divorce cases, where the parties have applied and the people's court has decided not to conduct an open trial;
   (6) Other cases that are not to be tried openly as otherwise provided by law.

For cases that are not tried openly, the reasons for not conducting an open trial shall be announced in court.

3. The following cases of second instance shall be tried openly:

   (1) Where a party files an appeal against a judgment or ruling of a first instance case that was tried openly, except for cases remanded for retrial due to violation of legal procedures, and cases where judgments or rulings are directly rendered according to law because the facts are clear.
   (2) Where a people's procuratorate files a protest against a judgment or ruling of a case that was tried openly, except for cases requiring remand for retrial.

4. For cases tried openly according to law, a notice shall be made three days before the court session. The notice shall include the cause of action, the names of the parties, the time and place of the court session.

5. For cases tried openly according to law, the facts of the case shall not be determined without open investigation in court.

   Evidence proving the facts of the case shall not be admitted as evidence without being presented and cross-examined openly in court, except for facts that do not require proof. For cases tried by default, the court may admit evidence in conjunction with other facts and evidence.

   If the court can admit evidence at the court session, it shall do so at such session.

6. All judgments of cases tried by the people's courts shall be pronounced publicly.

   When pronouncing a judgment, the facts and evidence of the case shall be determined, and on that basis, the law shall be correctly applied.

7. If a case that should have been tried openly according to law was not tried openly, it shall be handled according to the following provisions:

   (1) If a party files an appeal, or if a people's procuratorate files a protest against a criminal judgment or ruling, the people's court of second instance shall rule to set aside the original judgment and remand the case for retrial;
   (2) If a party applies for a retrial, the people's court may decide to conduct a retrial; if a people's procuratorate files a protest in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the people's court shall decide to conduct a retrial.

   The cases remanded for retrial or for which retrial is decided as mentioned above shall be tried openly according to law.

8. When the people's court tries a case openly, the court trial activities shall be conducted in the trial court. If it is necessary to conduct an open trial on circuit, an appropriate venue shall be selected.

9. The trial court and other venues where case trial activities are conducted openly shall display the national emblem and set up a bench for the judges and other corresponding seats in accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court regarding courtroom layout.

10. For cases tried openly according to law, citizens may attend the hearing as observers, except for persons with mental illnesses, intoxicated persons, and minors without the approval of the people's court.

    If, based on conditions such as the capacity of the courtroom and the number of observers, observers are required to hold observer passes to enter the courtroom, such passes shall be issued by the people's court.

    If foreigners or stateless persons request to attend the hearing with valid identification, the provisions applicable to Chinese citizens for attending hearings shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

    Observers must comply with the provisions of the "Rules of the People's Court of the People's Republic of China" and shall submit to security checks.

11. For cases tried openly according to law, with the permission of the people's court, journalists may take notes, make audio recordings, video recordings, take photographs, and broadcast the live trial proceedings. The attendance of foreign journalists at hearings shall be handled in accordance with relevant Chinese regulations on foreign affairs.

March 8, 1999
